abstract: Diagnosing a model's reasoning with an Activation Oracle (AO) requires reading trajectory-specific facts, not just problem-level gist. We test whether AO readers recover a local fact and what limits them, using exact ground truth. In real Qwen3-8B reasoning traces we replace every occurrence of a recent intermediate number with an unseen number of the same length. Edits are span-aligned. Three readers (original AO, GRPO-500, three-layer AO) answer "What number is the model working with right now?", scored with a unit-tested matcher. On 118 development pairs from 24 problems, a 5-position read centred on the number recovers the prefix's own number in 0.70, 0.76 and 0.65 of prefixes, +0.33 to +0.44 over a 50-position end window. In a pre-registered set built from the second most recent number (125 pairs, 33 problems), the gain holds for all three readers (+0.38 to +0.59). End windows fail in two ways: when the number lies outside the window, readers almost never report it (≤0.02); when it lies inside, they report it far less often than with a focused read. Appending the focused positions to the end window dilutes the fact again (−0.32 to −0.37, pre-registered, all readers). The edit changes the residual by about 0.6 at edited positions versus 0.02–0.08 elsewhere, and a problem-split probe decodes the number's last digit at layer 9 (0.80; baseline 0.16). Automatic localisation is the open bottleneck: the target model's attention finds the right digit token among its top five 72% of the time, but reading around its top choice gains only +0.03 to +0.07. Focused reads also collapse free-form descriptions, so practical readers must combine gist with located facts. A pre-registered AObench replication of the most recent number is underpowered and confirms the focus gain for one reader of three.
author: orthant_cartographer
change_summary:
Response to the rejection of GUpv0ipFLnXJsBmq.
(1) Matcher: replaced with a unit-tested number matcher (numutil.py: sentence punctuation allowed; decimals, adjacent digits and thousands separators excluded). All results were recomputed. The reader-gating conclusion is withdrawn (stated in §1): with correct scoring, all three readers report located numbers.
(2) Pairs: rebuilt with span-aligned edits (pairs_v2.py). Every integer occurrence in the final 400 characters is replaced, including sentence-final ones. Pairs are checked for no residual x, equal token length and differences confined to edited spans; the focus token is computed from span offsets and is identical in both arms. All experiments were rerun on the new pairs.
(3) New pre-registered evidence: a second-target set (125 pairs, 33 problems), where Q1 (focus > end50), Q2 (outside-window ~0) and Q3 (union < focus) hold for all three readers. The AObench most-recent-number replication is reported as partial (R1 1/3 readers; R2 not met, underpowered).
(4) Mechanism and scope: span-aligned activation distances replace the token-ID mask. The probe uses split-internal standardisation, a majority-digit baseline and split variability, and is framed as lexical recoverability of one attribute. The target ambiguity of the question is stated as a limitation. The unordered-integration interpretation was removed.
(5) Same union construction for numeric and free-form questions (end50 then focus5, 55 slots); free-form rerun for all three readers.
(6) Evidence: the supplement ships all pairs with alignment fields, all outputs, free-form annotations, locator picks and hits, distance records, layer-9 probe features, full held-out traces with continuations, the pre-registrations, and replay_local_v2.py, which regenerates §4.1-4.4. Section 4.5 is marked as context from earlier work.
title: Where is the fact? Local numbers in activation readout are readable when located, and missed or diluted by end windows
